why: How every client offers the ways to sign in to an account and says why a sign-in didn't work, as the box decides them (box/src/link/areas/sign-in.ts: kuvo/sign-in/methods and kuvo/sign-in/status's failure). Signing in with an account comes first, then credentials the computer already has (external), then a key, each kind in the engine's order; a way whose label says legacy comes after all the others, marked legacy; a plan that goes through a coding agent (ChatGPT's, SuperGrok's) isn't offered for the engine's provider unless it's signed in that way already. `offered` is kuvo/sign-in/methods' answer, and each account's in kuvo/sign-in/accounts, with `hint`, the way in its card names (its first sign-in that isn't legacy, "Login with" said "Sign in with", plain "Sign in" where it only names the account again; else "API key" for a key; else "Connect"). Clients draw it as it is, and show `failure` as it is. Methods shaped as engine 2.2.5 lists them (api/integration): openai, xai, deepseek and github-copilot as it lists them; the others made up to hold each rule. The phone's sample Mac and its tests' computers serve these answers as recorded, matched by provider, name, methods and connections. `accounts`: what each account kuvo/sign-in/accounts lists is (`kind`), whether Accounts lists it (`listed`), and its mark by the plan limits' service ids (`service`; none: its letter), for the engine's or, with `agents`, the coding agents' bridge's (#711). `codes`: the code a device sign-in's page asks for (`userCode` in kuvo/sign-in/start's and kuvo/sign-in/status's answers), from what the engine or the bridge said of the attempt; none where it has none. `states`: whether an account is a plan you sign in to (`plan`: one of its ways in, as the box offers them, is its sign-in page; a key or the computer's credentials isn't), how an account stands, the line under its name, each of its sign-ins and what can be done with it (box/src/link/areas/sign-in-state.ts: kuvo/sign-in/accounts' state, line, connections and actions), from the account as the engine or the bridge lists it (`agents`), its ways in as the box offers them (`offered`, as `methods` above), the saved sign-in the box saw end (`ended`) and the box's computer's name (`computer`). An account whose only way in is a key is entered, never signed into: its buttons say Add Key, Replace Key and Add Another Key (#733).
